evidence.claim: The Lebanon Cornwall Scenic Byway follows PA 419 from Quentin to the Berks County line, passing rolling farmland and Amish communities.
evidence.quote: the Lebanon Cornwall Scenic Byway starts in Quentin at the intersection of Routes 419 and 72 and follows Route 419 to the Berks County line.

evidence.claim: It is a two-lane, undivided road through rural country, with farmland and woodland giving way to residential streets in its towns.
evidence.quote: PA 419 is a two-lane undivided road its entire length and passes through rural areas.

evidence.claim: The Quentin-to-Cornwall stretch once carried US 322.
evidence.quote: In the 1930s, US 322 replaced the PA 5 designation that ran concurrent with PA 72 between Quentin and Cornwall.

evidence.claim: That highway moved onto a bypass in 1963; by 1966, PA 419 had been designated along its present alignment.
evidence.quote: In 1963, US 322 was shifted to bypass Cornwall along with PA 72, removing it from the road that ran between Quentin and Cornwall. PA 419 was designated by 1966

evidence.claim: PennDOT records 2008 as the effective year of the Lebanon Cornwall Byway designation, covering the road from PA 72 at Quentin to the county line.
evidence.quote: LEBANON CORNWALL BYWAY Effective: 2008 District: 8-0 County: Lebanon State Route: 419 Starts in Lebanon County, at the Intersection of Route 419 and 72 (Quentin) and ends at the Berks County Line on 419.

evidence.claim: Begin at Quentin and head east through Cornwall on Freeman Drive.
evidence.quote: The road continues into the borough of Cornwall and becomes Freeman Drive

evidence.claim: After crossing the Lebanon Valley Rail Trail, the road turns northeast and becomes Schaeffer Road through agricultural country.
evidence.quote: PA 419 crosses the Lebanon Valley Rail Trail before it turns to the northeast and enters South Lebanon Township, where the name becomes Schaeffer Road and it continues east through agricultural areas

evidence.claim: In Schaefferstown, it shares Heidelberg Avenue with PA 897, then turns north on North Market Street.
evidence.quote: PA 419 splits from PA 897 by turning north onto North Market Street

evidence.claim: Beyond town, the route curves through farmland to Millbach and Newmanstown’s Main Street before reaching Berks County.
evidence.quote: The route curves east through more agricultural land before turning northeast again and passing through the communities of Millbach Springs and Millbach. PA 419 heads into the community of Newmanstown, where it is called Main Street and is lined with homes.

evidence.claim: Quentin’s name commemorates a young fighter pilot killed in the First World War.
evidence.quote: In October 1920, the name was changed to honor Quentin Roosevelt, who was killed while flying as a fighter pilot during World War I.

evidence.claim: Until October 1920, the village was Bismark, a local spelling of Otto von Bismarck’s name.
evidence.quote: The town was originally named "Bismark", a local spelling of the name of Otto von Bismarck.

evidence.claim: The new name honored Quentin Roosevelt, President Theodore Roosevelt’s youngest son.
evidence.quote: It was named after Quentin Roosevelt, youngest son of President Theodore Roosevelt.

evidence.claim: PA 419 passes through the community’s center, while PA 72 runs through its eastern side.
evidence.quote: Pennsylvania Route 72 runs through the eastern side of Quentin

evidence.claim: Their intersection marks the start of the designated byway; Cornwall borders Quentin to the east.

evidence.claim: Cornwall borders Quentin to the east.

evidence.claim: At Cornwall, iron ore lay at or close to the surface, with timber, limestone and running water available for smelting.
evidence.quote: Namely, vast stands of timber for the production of charcoal, running water to operate the bellows, and an ample supply of limestone needed to add flux to the smelting furnaces.

evidence.claim: Peter Grubb established the furnace in 1742.
evidence.quote: Established by Peter Grubb in 1742

evidence.claim: The works depended on free laborers, indentured servants and enslaved people.
evidence.quote: There were three groups of workers at Cornwall Iron Furnace: Free labor, indentured servants and slaves.

evidence.claim: A steam engine replaced the waterwheel in 1841, and the furnace stack was rebuilt in the 1850s.
evidence.quote: The waterwheel was replaced by a steam engine in 1841. And the furnace stack was rebuilt in the 1850s.

evidence.claim: Production ended in 1883.
evidence.quote: The furnace was a leading Pennsylvania iron producer from 1742 until it was shut down in 1883.

evidence.claim: The preserved furnace and support buildings now form a historical site and museum, making the scale of the operation legible beyond the furnace itself.
evidence.quote: The furnaces, support buildings and surrounding community have been preserved as a historical site and museum, providing a glimpse into Lebanon County's industrial past.

evidence.claim: Water still reaches Schaefferstown households through the system Alexander Schaeffer constructed between 1744 and 1750.
evidence.quote: The water system was constructed sometime between 1744 and 1750 by the founder of the town, Alexander Schaeffer.

evidence.claim: Located in what is now Fountain Park, it carries water by gravity through underground pipes.
evidence.quote: The water company in Schaefferstown has the oldest gravitational conveyance system by underground pipes in the United States.

evidence.claim: The original system supplied two wooden troughs on the square at Main and Market streets.
evidence.quote: When the original system was laid out, it ran to two wooden troughs on the Square, which is now the intersection of Main Street and Market Street.

evidence.claim: Matilda Zimmerman later replaced one trough in memory of her mother, Mary Rex Zimmerman, a great-granddaughter of Schaeffer.
evidence.quote: One trough was since replaced by Matilda Zimmerman in memory of Mary Rex Zimmerman, her mother and great granddaughter of Alexander Schaeffer.

evidence.claim: That replacement stands on the south face of the historic bank in the square.
evidence.quote: This trough is now located on the south face of the historic bank located within the Square.

evidence.claim: Water still reaches Schaefferstown households
evidence.quote: The water system, which is located in the area now known as Fountain Park, is still used by the townspeople for potable household water.

evidence.claim: PennDOT also records a prohibition on off-premise signs, enforced through local ordinances along this designated stretch.
evidence.quote: The prohibition of off-premise signs is enforced by local ordinances.

evidence.claim: The road between Cornwall and Schaefferstown was paved by 1930, before the present route number linked these communities.
evidence.quote: By 1930, the road between Cornwall and Schaefferstown along with the entire length of PA 483 were paved.
